terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to see the tags, the pick of the month and the copies it makes.

tasks.title: Print a shelf tag
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/destructuring.js`, make `shelfTag(candle)` pull `name`, `grams` and `priceCents` out of the card by name, with destructuring, and return them as one line: `'Cedar, 200 g, 1800 cents'`. When the card has no `grams`, the tag shows `200 g`: give `grams` a default of `200` where you pull it out.

Check calls `shelfTag` with cards of its own, old ones with no grams included, and reads your file for the destructuring and the default.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on pulling properties out and on defaults.
Write one line that makes `name`, `grams` and `priceCents` from the card.
Give `grams` its default inside the braces.
Return the tag and run the file: the old fig card should show 200 g.
hints: Destructuring makes several variables from one object in one line, each named after a key.
The names in the braces must match the keys of the card. A default goes right after a name, with `=`, and is used when the card has no such property.
The first line is `const { name, grams = 200, priceCents } = candle`, then a template literal with the three names.

tasks.title: Pick the candle of the month
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, `monthPick(names)` is given a list of candle names with at least one name in it. The first name is the candle of the month and the others are the runners-up. Pull the first name out with destructuring and collect the others with rest, then return the first name, the word `and`, the number of runners-up and the word `more`: `'Fig and 2 more'`. The list stays as it is.

Check calls `monthPick` with lists of its own, one with a single name included, and reads your file for the destructuring.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on taking lists apart and on rest.
Write one line that makes the first name and a list of the others.
Return the text and run the file.
hints: Square brackets on the left of `=` take a list apart by position, the way curly braces take an object apart by key.
Three dots before the last name collect everything that is left into a new list. With one name, that list is empty.
The first line is `const [first, ...others] = names`, then the text uses `first` and `others.length`.

tasks.title: Change the price on a copy
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `withPrice(candle, priceCents)` return a new card: a copy of `candle` with every property it has, except that its `priceCents` is the one given. The card it was given stays as it is.

Check calls `withPrice` with cards of its own, some with properties the others do not have, and makes sure each card it gave is unchanged afterwards.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on copying an object with a change.
Make a new object that spreads the card's properties into it.
Give the new object its new price, after the spread.
Run the file: the second line shows the cedar card, with its old price.
hints: Changing `candle.priceCents` changes the shop's own card. Make a new object instead.
Three dots inside the curly braces of a new object copy every property of another object into it. When a key appears twice, the one written last wins.
The function is one line: `return { ...candle, priceCents }`, or `priceCents: priceCents`.

tasks.title: Hide what a candle costs us
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, first write a function of your own called `publicCard`, from the word `function` to its closing brace. It has one parameter, `candle`, and returns a new card with every property of `candle` except `costCents`, which the site must never show. It only helps `publicCatalogue`, so it stays off the `export` line.

Then make `publicCatalogue(candles)` return a new list with the public card of every candle in the list, in the same order, made by `publicCard`. The list and its cards stay as they are.

Check calls `publicCard` and `publicCatalogue` with cards of its own, and reads your file for `publicCard` and the use of it inside `publicCatalogue`. A left out property must be gone, not just hold `undefined`.
nextSteps: Above `publicCatalogue`, write `function publicCard(candle) {` and its closing `}` yourself.
Pull `costCents` out of the card and collect the rest into a new object.
Return the rest, then make `publicCatalogue` build a new list with `publicCard`.
Run the file: no card in the last line shows costCents.
hints: Deleting `costCents` from the card itself would take it off the shop's own card too.
Rest works in curly braces as well: name the key you want out, and three dots before a last name collect every other property into a new object. `map` makes a new list from another.
`publicCard` can be `const { costCents, ...shown } = candle` then `return shown`, and `publicCatalogue` is `return candles.map(publicCard)`.
